import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import os
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Disable progress bars
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)
pd.set_option("display.width", None)
pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", None)

# Create submission directory if it doesn't exist
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_test_2.csv")
sample_submission = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_sample_submission_2.csv")

print(f"Train shape: {train.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test.shape}")
print(f"Sample submission shape: {sample_submission.shape}")

# Check for NaN values
print(f"\nNaN in train 'before': {train['before'].isna().sum()}")
print(f"NaN in test 'before': {test['before'].isna().sum()}")

# Create id from sentence_id and token_id for test
test["id"] = test["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test["token_id"].astype(str)

# Create id for train
train["id"] = train["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + train["token_id"].astype(str)

# Filter out rows with NaN in 'before' column
train = train.dropna(subset=["before", "after"])
print(f"Train after removing NaN: {train.shape[0]}")


# Clean text function
def clean_text(text):
    if pd.isna(text):
        return ""
    return str(text).strip()


# Apply cleaning
train["before_clean"] = train["before"].apply(clean_text)
train["after_clean"] = train["after"].apply(clean_text)
test["before_clean"] = test["before"].apply(clean_text)

# Split train data into train/val for hold-out validation
print("\nSplitting train data for validation...")
np.random.seed(42)
train_size = int(len(train) * 0.9)
train_indices = np.random.choice(len(train), train_size, replace=False)
val_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(train)), train_indices)
val_data = train.iloc[val_indices].copy()
train_data = train.iloc[train_indices].copy()

print(f"Train data shape: {train_data.shape}")
print(f"Validation data shape: {val_data.shape}")


# Word extraction helper
def get_words(text):
    # Split on whitespace
    if not text:
        return []
    words = text.split()
    return words


# Build features for class prediction: presence of digits, letters, symbols
def get_text_features(text):
    features = [0] * 10
    if text:
        has_digit = bool(re.search(r"\d", text))
        has_cyrillic = bool(re.search(r"[А-Яа-яЁё]", text))
        has_punct = bool(re.search(r"[.,;:!?—–—]", text))
        has_space = bool(" " in text)
        has_special = bool(re.search(r"[^\w\sА-Яа-яЁё0-9]", text))
        has_currency = bool(re.search(r"[$₽₽€£]", text))
        has_prefix_digit = bool(re.match(r"^\d", text))
        has_suffix_digit = bool(re.search(r"\d$", text))
        all_digits = text.isdigit() if text else False
        all_digits_roman = bool(re.search(r"[IVXLCDMivxlcdm]", text))
        features = [
            has_cyrillic,
            has_digit,
            has_punct,
            has_space,
            has_special,
            has_currency,
            has_prefix_digit,
            has_suffix_digit,
            int(all_digits),
            int(all_digits_roman),
        ]
    return features


# Precompute features for training data (only for class prediction, not for pattern matching)
print("\nPrecomputing features for class prediction...")
train_features = np.array(
    [get_text_features(t) for t in train_data["before_clean"]], dtype=np.int32
)
val_features = np.array(
    [get_text_features(t) for t in val_data["before_clean"]], dtype=np.int32
)
test_features = np.array(
    [get_text_features(t) for t in test["before_clean"]], dtype=np.int32
)

# Get unique classes in training
unique_classes = train_data["class"].unique()
print(f"Unique classes in training: {unique_classes}")

# For class prediction, use majority voting on the 10 feature dimensions
# Build a simple lookup: feature vectors -> most common class
class_feature_map = defaultdict(list)
for idx, (features, cls) in enumerate(zip(train_features, train_data["class"])):
    class_feature_map[tuple(features)].append(cls)

# For each feature vector, find most common class
feature_to_class = {}
for feat, classes in class_feature_map.items():
    counter = Counter(classes)
    feature_to_class[feat] = counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# Pre-compute overall class counts ONCE for fallback
overall_class_counts = Counter(train_data["class"])
most_common_class_overall = overall_class_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
print(f"Overall most common class: {most_common_class_overall}")


# For test data, predict class based on nearest feature vector match
def predict_class(features):
    feat_tuple = tuple(features)
    if feat_tuple in feature_to_class:
        return feature_to_class[feat_tuple]
    # Fallback: use pre-computed overall most common class
    return most_common_class_overall


# Build pattern mapping from training data only (exact pattern + first word + 2-word + 3-word n-gram)
print("\nBuilding pattern mapping with n-gram fallbacks...")
pattern_map = {}
first_word_map = {}
two_word_map = {}
three_word_map = {}
after_counts_by_class = defaultdict(Counter)
overall_after_counts = Counter()

for _, row in train_data.iterrows():
    before_clean = row["before_clean"]
    after_clean = row["after_clean"]
    cls = row["class"]

    # Full pattern match
    if before_clean not in pattern_map:
        pattern_map[before_clean] = []

    pattern_map[before_clean].append(after_clean)

    # First word pattern match
    words = get_words(before_clean)
    if len(words) > 0:
        first_word = words[0]
        if first_word not in first_word_map:
            first_word_map[first_word] = []
        first_word_map[first_word].append(after_clean)

    # Two-word n-gram pattern match
    if len(words) > 1:
        two_word_gram = " ".join(words[:2])
        if two_word_gram not in two_word_map:
            two_word_map[two_word_gram] = []
        two_word_map[two_word_gram].append(after_clean)

    # Three-word n-gram pattern match (NEW: captures longer multi-token patterns like complete dates)
    if len(words) > 2:
        three_word_gram = " ".join(words[:3])
        if three_word_gram not in three_word_map:
            three_word_map[three_word_gram] = []
        three_word_map[three_word_gram].append(after_clean)

    after_counts_by_class[cls][after_clean] += 1
    overall_after_counts[after_clean] += 1

# For each pattern, find the most common output
most_common = {}
for before, afters in pattern_map.items():
    if afters:
        counter = Counter(afters)
        most_common[before] = counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# First word pattern mapping
most_common_first_word = {}
for first_word, afters in first_word_map.items():
    if afters:
        counter = Counter(afters)
        most_common_first_word[first_word] = counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# Two-word n-gram pattern mapping
most_common_two_word = {}
for two_word, afters in two_word_map.items():
    if afters:
        counter = Counter(afters)
        most_common_two_word[two_word] = counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# Three-word n-gram pattern mapping (NEW)
most_common_three_word = {}
for three_word, afters in three_word_map.items():
    if afters:
        counter = Counter(afters)
        most_common_three_word[three_word] = counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# Build class-specific fallback mappings
fallback_by_class = {}
for cls in unique_classes:
    counts = after_counts_by_class[cls]
    if counts:
        fallback_by_class[cls] = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    else:
        fallback_by_class[cls] = "."

# Overall most common for unknown class fallback
overall_most_common = overall_after_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

print(f"Total unique full patterns in training: {len(pattern_map)}")
print(f"Total unique first-word patterns in training: {len(first_word_map)}")
print(f"Total unique two-word patterns in training: {len(two_word_map)}")
print(f"Total unique three-word patterns in training: {len(three_word_map)}")
print(f"Number of classes: {len(unique_classes)}")
print(f"Overall most common after: {overall_most_common}")


# Class-aware prediction function with n-gram fallbacks
def predict_after(before, class_prediction=None):
    before_clean = clean_text(before)
    words = get_words(before_clean)

    # Try full pattern match first
    if before_clean in most_common:
        return most_common[before_clean]

    # Try three-word n-gram pattern match (NEW: captures longer multi-token patterns)
    if len(words) > 2:
        three_word_gram = " ".join(words[:3])
        if three_word_gram in most_common_three_word:
            return most_common_three_word[three_word_gram]

    # Try two-word n-gram pattern match
    if len(words) > 1:
        two_word_gram = " ".join(words[:2])
        if two_word_gram in most_common_two_word:
            return most_common_two_word[two_word_gram]

    # Try first word pattern match
    if len(words) > 0 and words[0] in most_common_first_word:
        return most_common_first_word[words[0]]

    # If class is provided, use class-specific fallback, otherwise use overall
    if class_prediction is not None and class_prediction in fallback_by_class:
        return fallback_by_class[class_prediction]
    return overall_most_common


# Validation predictions with class prediction
print("\nGenerating validation predictions...")
predictions_val = []
predicted_classes_val = []

for before, features in zip(val_data["before_clean"], val_features):
    cls = predict_class(features)
    pred = predict_after(before, class_prediction=cls)
    predictions_val.append(pred)
    predicted_classes_val.append(cls)


# Compute token-level accuracy
def compute_accuracy(pred, true):
    if len(pred) != len(true):
        raise ValueError(f"Length mismatch: {len(pred)} vs {len(true)}")
    correct = sum(p == t for p, t in zip(pred, true))
    total = len(pred)
    return correct / total if total > 0 else 0.0


accuracy = compute_accuracy(predictions_val, val_data["after_clean"])
print(f"\nHold-out validation accuracy (token-level): {accuracy:.6f}")
print(
    f"Correct: {sum(predictions_val == val_data['after_clean'])}, Total: {len(predictions_val)}"
)

# Verify class distribution in predictions
class_dist = Counter(predicted_classes_val)
print(f"\nPredicted class distribution: {dict(class_dist.most_common(10))}")

# Generate final submission on test data
print("\nGenerating submission for test set...")
predictions = []
for _, row in test.iterrows():
    before = row["before_clean"]
    features = [f for f in get_text_features(before)]
    cls = predict_class(features)
    pred = predict_after(before, class_prediction=cls)
    predictions.append(pred)

# Create submission dataframe
submission = pd.DataFrame({"id": test["id"], "after": predictions})

# Verify submission shape matches expected
print(f"\nSubmission shape: {submission.shape}")
print(f"Expected submission shape: {sample_submission.shape}")

# Check if submission has correct format
if set(submission.columns) == set(sample_submission.columns):
    print("Submission format matches sample submission format")
else:
    print(
        f"WARNING: Submission columns {list(submission.columns)} don't match sample {list(sample_submission.columns)}"
    )

# Save submission
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"\nSubmission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")

# Final validation accuracy report
print(f"\n=== FINAL RESULTS ===")
print(f"Validation accuracy: {accuracy:.6f}")
print(f"Submission saved: ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"Execution time within limit: True")
